professional_summary.short_bio: I design and implement game audio — Wwise integration, C++ audio systems, and Unreal Engine.
professional_summary.extended_bio: I spent 12 years studying classical piano, but I was always more curious about why sound works than how to perform it. That curiosity took me from music school through physics and maths, and eventually into game audio. Now I design sounds and write the C++ and Python tools that make them run in real-time.
professional_summary.philosophy: A gunshot that sounds amazing but causes a frame drop is a bad sound. Audio has to work within CPU and memory budgets — that's non-negotiable.

featured_projects.title: Transientica: AudioLab
featured_projects.tagline: Control a rhythm game with your voice
featured_projects.short_description: Beatbox into your mic, play a rhythm game. Real-time ML recognition with under 60ms latency.
featured_projects.detailed_description: Voice-controlled rhythm game using ML beatbox recognition. 92% accurate across 450 test samples, 45-60ms latency. You train it with 30 examples of each drum sound, then play. Python/scikit-learn handles the ML, Unity handles gameplay.

technical_achievements.pipeline: Spectral-flux onset detection into SVM classification
technical_achievements.optimization: Small FFT window (512 samples, 11ms), circular buffer to kill I/O blocking, lightweight SVM (2ms vs 15ms for a neural net)
technical_achievements.architecture: Audio and ML on separate threads, lock-free ringbuffer, audio pinned to high-priority thread

challenges_solved.problem: First version had 180ms lag — way too slow for a rhythm game
challenges_solved.solution: Shrunk the FFT window, added a circular buffer, swapped to a lightweight SVM, and switched to UDP for OSC. Got it down to 45ms at 92% accuracy

challenges_solved.problem: Both have sharp transients and broadband noise — the classifier kept guessing wrong
challenges_solved.solution: Added spectral centroid, zero-crossing rate, and envelope shape as features. Built separate models for solo hits vs patterns. Accuracy went from 78% to 92%

challenges_solved.problem: Heavy ML processing caused buffer underruns on slower machines
challenges_solved.solution: Separated threads with a lock-free ringbuffer. Audio never blocks, ML runs on its own worker thread

featured_projects.full_description:
Real-time beatbox recognition that lets you control a rhythm game with your voice.

I optimized the audio buffers and ML pipeline to stay under 60ms latency. Python handles the audio analysis, Unity handles gameplay, and they talk over UDP/OSC.

code_snippets.title: Real-time Inference Loop (Python)
code_snippets.description: Audio buffer processing and SVM classification.
code_snippets.code:
def audio_callback(indata, frames, time, status):
    if status:
        print(status)
    
    # Add new data to ring buffer
    ring_buffer.extend(indata[:, 0])
    
    # Extract features
    features = extract_features(list(ring_buffer)[-BUFFER_SIZE:])
    
    # Predict
    prediction = model.predict([features])[0]
    
    # Send OSC if confidence high
    if prediction != 'silence':
        client.send_message("/beatbox/trigger", prediction)

code_snippets.title: Clean & Rebuild Logic (Batch)
code_snippets.description: Automates the deletion of intermediate/derived data caches to force a clean engine rebuild.
code_snippets.code:
@echo off
echo Cleaning Unreal Engine Intermediate Files...

RMDIR /S /Q "Intermediate"
RMDIR /S /Q "Binaries"
RMDIR /S /Q "DerivedDataCache"
RMDIR /S /Q "Saved"

echo Regenerating Project Files...
"%UE5_ENGINE_PATH%\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat" -project="%PROJECT_PATH%" -progress

echo Build Complete.
pause
